newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemeni president vows poll will be fair and safe.
newsitem.headline: Yemeni president vows poll will be fair and safe.

text.p: Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh on Tuesday assured international observers the country's upcoming elections would be free, fair and safe.

Speaking to a group of about 70 observers, Saleh said the parliamentary elections on Sunday -- the first since a civil war in 1994 -- "will be free and democratic...and will take place in a fair, safe and secure environment".

"There is an unfair, anti-democratic information campaign in Yemen and some are expecting that there will be unrest and violence. This is not correct...All security measures have been adopted (to ensure a safe poll)," he said.
On Monday a Yemeni man was killed and several were hurt in pre-election clashes between supporters of Yemen's ruling General Peoples Congress party and its Islah party coalition partner.
There have been frequent clashes between backers of various parties in the run-up to the poll, but there had been no previous casualties.
The head of Yemen's security committee for the elections said earlier this month that some 60,000 police and troops would be deployed across Yemen to boost election security.
Saleh also told the observers they could monitor the poll in any constituency they wished. More than 150 international observers are due to monitor the poll.
Election officials expect about 5,000 candidates to seek votes for 301 parliamentary seats under the banners of 12 parties or as independents.
